procedure:while the Codex seats have no network (D-024-36), the orchestrator does not run `gh pr update-branch` on a Codex worker's PR while that worker has unpushed work; the update-branch merge makes the worker's next head a non-fast-forward and forces a local merge round trip (a013 on #437 at 08:0xZ, a012 on #440 at 2026-10-20T09:34Z); update-branch happens when the chain starts on the transported head.

procedure:a task text that makes an environment input mandatory on the checker side (an `absolute-cache requirement`, a mandatory `TRUSTED_*`) while authorizing no caller edit breaks the callers on main (regime-ci.py's checker launch, the regime workflow, the pre-send glue: six RegimeCiTest failures on #440 head b8bf8066); such a text names the on-main caller tests that must stay green (tests/unit/test_regime_ci.py) and prefers a checker-side default (a private temporary cache) over a caller obligation; pre-send.sh fails a text that holds both a mandatory-environment sentence (UV_CACHE_DIR, TRUSTED_*) and a no-caller-edit sentence (M-20261020-04)

mechanism:`.agents/worklog/orchestrator-glue/result-evidence-check.sh <task> <head40> [<pr>]` runs before the orchestrator judges any RESULT: it refuses a validation.md whose full-suite candidate failures+errors exceed the base without each extra test named, and (with <pr>) a head whose CI runs are not all concluded green; the a06 RESULT of b8bf8066 (candidate 156 vs base 150 failures, sent 09:42Z before the run ended 09:45Z) is refused by it (M-20261020-04); promotion into scripts/orchestrator/ follows the pre-send-check-a01 pattern as a task

mechanism:the prose-row to JSON-ledger mapping of D-024-42 (`<kind>:<sha7>:<n>` -> `audit:<sha7>:<n>`) collided across kinds on one head (ci, worker and security rows of b8bf806 collapsed to one id; 3 collisions in the a06 record, 3 in worker-write-boundary-a02), so the JSON ledger undercounted classes and the gate's S1 could pass silently; record-json-sync.py now maps injectively with a per-kind offset (audit 0, ci 100, worker 200, security 300, text-security 400, local 500, orchestrator-text 600), accepts digit-bearing class slugs, and `--rebuild` drops the old audit ids and re-adds every prose row; the proper fix is a provenance slot in the gate grammar (`(audit|ci|worker|security|text-security|local|orchestrator-text):<sha7>:<n>` in scripts/require-crit-review.py and acceptance-front-matter.py), a task (M-20261020-05)

procedure:a chain step that calls a review model has a wall-clock cap; the #432 chain's local review (`codex review --base main`) ran 61 minutes with no output after a network outage (the #442 review took 4m48s) and the chain never notified; until local-review.sh and chain-integrate.sh carry `timeout` (a worker task), the orchestrator starts every chain under a 3600-second alarm (`perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 3600 chain-integrate.sh …`; no timeout binary exists on this host) and records the elapsed time of each step from the chain log

mechanism:a new task id is checked against the existing lineages before any authoring: pre-send.sh refuses a text whose `.orchestration/acceptance/<task_id>.md` or `.orchestration/tasks/<task_id>.md` already exists unless the text carries `previous_sha256:` (an amendment) or `reset_of:` (a reset); the orchestrator chose `dotfiles-T133-result-precheck-a01` for a new mechanism while that id is plan 024 P1-5's lineage (a01 withdrawn 10-18, a04 on PR #411) and `cp` overwrote the dispatched a01 text (restored from HEAD, byte-identical check by sha); the new lineage is `dotfiles-T133-result-evidence-check-a01` and the glue `result-evidence-check.sh` (M-20261020-06)

mechanism:every chain, audit or security-review invocation takes its task id from `pr-task.sh <pr>` (the PR head's `.orchestration/<task>/task.md` whose record names the PR, highest suffix), never from the branch name or memory; the #432 chain ran twice under the superseded a02 id and wrote into the a02 record and validation files (restored from HEAD; M-20261020-07)

mechanism:every TASK dispatch goes through `send-task.sh <team> <from> <to> <pane> <task.md> <line-file>`, which runs pre-send.sh on the text and the line, refuses on any non-zero exit, checks that the line's `task_sha256=` equals the text's sha256, and only then calls dispatch.sh; the orchestrator never calls dispatch.sh directly for a TASK line again. Cause: the worker-sandbox-exclusions-a01 TASK (2840) was dispatched after pre-send had refused the text (`over self cap: refused`, 129 lines against 125) because the shell step read pre-send's output with `tail` and ignored its exit code (M-20261020-08, the second occurrence of the M-20261020-03 class)

mechanism:an ACCEPTANCE status=revise goes through send-task.sh too and carries either amendment=N (the text changed, hashed) or text=unchanged (send-task verifies the text's sha256 equals the last dispatched TASK's task_sha256); the #436 revise 1 changed a text requirement (passwd_home) without an amendment and cost a records-only round that pushed the lineage to S2 (audit:a561e64:3, the trusted-exec a02 reset); text-security-review.sh refuses security: false texts (C-80 scope, D-024-46); briefs carry BRIEF-TEMPLATE-NOTES.md items 1-5
